text.tspan: Option 3, the way IN to VPC B: four load balancer set-ups in the unique routable subnet
A · Internal ALB (layer 7): HTTP only, simplest
B · NLB → controller (NLB = door, controller = receptionist)
C · NLB, one listener per port (non-HTTP)
D · NLB → ALB (fixed IPs + layer-7 rules)
The ALB routes by host and path itself. Its IPs change as it scales,
so clients use its DNS name.
One NLB, many services. The NLB never reads names; the routes
(HTTPRoute or Ingress) live in the controller. TLS passthrough works.
Routing by port only. Each target group is bound to its Service with
For when firewall rules need fixed IPs
but you still want ALB routing rules.
Rule: an NLB is layer 4 and routes only by listener port. Host or path routing always happens in a layer-7 hop:
an ALB, or an ingress / gateway controller. Fewer load balancers = lower cost and fewer IPs used in the small routable CIDR.
